violated_contract: A dependency version range written with an inclusive upper bound ([a,b]) admits b. When the vendor publishes that next major, the build resolves it with no repository change, and a third-party plugin compiled against the previous major stops compiling, so every job that configures the build fails at once. The range reads as a ceiling but is not one.
canonical_prevention: Declare the dependency with a direct `strictly` range whose upper bound is exclusive, so the next major is rejected even when a transitive plugin declares the same inclusive range; a direct strictly range wins over a transitive one, which a plain version or an inclusive range cannot do. Assert the exclusive ceiling in a static guard so it cannot drift back to an inclusive bound.
